---
title: "Color and links in terminal output"
description: "Control whether q2 colors its messages and makes file paths clickable, with the --color option and the standard NO_COLOR, CLICOLOR, and FORCE_COLOR environment variables."
---

## Overview

When `q2` prints errors, warnings, and log messages to a terminal, it colors
them and turns file locations into clickable links. When the output goes
somewhere else, such as a file, a pipe, or a CI log, `q2` prints plain text,
so logs stay readable and easy to search:

```sh
q2 render index.qmd 2> render.log   # render.log contains plain text
```

`q2` makes this choice separately for standard output and standard error.

## The `--color` option

`--color` overrides the automatic choice for a single run. It works with
every command and can go before or after the command name:

```sh
q2 render index.qmd --color=never    # never color
q2 --color=always render index.qmd   # always color, even into a file
q2 render index.qmd --color=auto     # the default: decide automatically
```

`--color=always` does not add clickable links when the output is not a
terminal. Links in a log file are noise, not something you can click.

## Environment variables

`q2` follows the common conventions for these variables, so a setting you
already use for other tools also applies to `q2`.

| Variable | Effect |
|----------|--------|
| `NO_COLOR` | Set to any non-empty value: no color and no links. See [no-color.org](https://no-color.org). |
| `CLICOLOR_FORCE`, `FORCE_COLOR` | Set to a non-empty value other than `0`: color even when the output is not a terminal. Useful in CI systems whose log viewers show color. |
| `CLICOLOR` | Set to `0`: no color. |
| `FORCE_HYPERLINK` | Set to `1`: always emit clickable links. Set to `0`: never emit them. |
| `TERM` | Set to `dumb`: no color. |

## Which setting wins

When several settings apply, the first match in this list decides:

1. The `--color` option.
2. `NO_COLOR`.
3. `CLICOLOR_FORCE` or `FORCE_COLOR`.
4. `CLICOLOR=0`.
5. Whether the output is a terminal that supports color.

For example, `NO_COLOR=1 q2 render --color=always` prints color, because the
option comes first. `NO_COLOR=1 CLICOLOR_FORCE=1 q2 render` prints plain
text.

## Clickable links

`q2` emits clickable file links only when color is on, the output is a
terminal, and `q2` recognizes the terminal as one that supports links.
Recognized terminals include iTerm2, WezTerm, Ghostty, kitty, Alacritty,
Windows Terminal, Konsole, GNOME Terminal and other VTE-based terminals,
and the VS Code terminal. Inside a terminal multiplexer such as tmux,
or in a terminal `q2` does not recognize, set `FORCE_HYPERLINK=1` if your
terminal does support links.

## Help output

`q2 --help` follows the environment variables above, but not the `--color`
option.
